evidence: The SOI 2025 layer shows the same 13 Andhra Pradesh districts as the 2021 layer (Anantapur, Chittoor, East Godavari, Guntur, Krishna, Kurnool, Potti Sriramulu Nellore, Prakasam, Srikakulam, Visakhapatnam, Vizianagaram, West Godavari, Y S R Kadapa). The events compilation dates a reorganisation to 2022 with 16 events naming 24 successor districts, the 13 new ones listed here and existing ones under new names (Nellore, YSR), none of which matches any district on any map (outputs/audit/credibility_map_lag.csv). Recorded from the events compilation and the map alone; CONFIRMED needs a second independent source (a gazette notification). No MERGED_INTO edge results, so V19 is unaffected: the map simply never splits these districts, and statistics harmonized onto '2025 districts' in this state land on the 13 pre-2022 units.

The SOI 2025 layer has the same 8 Mizoram districts as the pre-2018 map (Aizawl, Champhai, Kolasib, Lawngtlai, Lunglei, Mamit, Saiha, Serchhip). Khawzawl (from Champhai) and Saitual (from Aizawl) are absent, though the events compilation dates both to 2019; Hnahthial is absent from the events compilation entirely, a gap in that source, not the map. Wikidata carries separate items for all three (Khawzawl Q86882591, Saitual Q86882593, Hnahthial Q86882590), each with distinct coordinates, confirming they are recognised as separate current entities, though Wikidata records no inception date for them. Unlike the Assam 1981 case, this is not a mislabelled vintage (the 2025 map is not secretly depicting some other single year): it is a real gap in SOI's latest boundary update for one state. lib.depicted_year is not used here because it must stay monotonic with the map's own vintage ordering (s11 CHECK depicted_year >= year; s09 window selection assumes d(a) < event_year <= d(b)), and Mizoram's 2021 vintage already shows Khawzawl and Saitual as separate CKs -- asserting the 2025 vintage depicts an earlier year would invert that ordering. This table exists instead of forcing the gap into vintage_depiction.csv. It explains, but does not silence, the 3 MERGED_INTO edges into the 2025 Champhai CK in s05 lineage (see CLAUDE.md Open items and outputs/pipeline/s05_district_relationship.csv).

The SOI 2025 layer shows 33 Rajasthan districts, the same number as the 2011 and 2021 layers. The events compilation dates the creation of the 15 districts listed here to 2023 (13 events); none matches any district on any map (outputs/audit/credibility_map_lag.csv). Recorded from the events compilation and the map alone; CONFIRMED needs a second independent source. Whether each of these districts still exists at the 2025 map's date is not established by this repository and must be checked against the notifications before any is treated as current.
